name: FOLFIRI (simplified, Andre)

drugs.name: Irinotecan
drugs.notes: DeVita 12th ed., Cancer of the Colon, Table 40.12 (line 123595): FOLFIRI (simplified) per Andre et al. 1999 - Irinotecan 180 mg/m2 over 90 min, day 1 only.

drugs.name: Leucovorin
drugs.route: IV concurrent with irinotecan (may run through same line via Y-connector)
drugs.notes: DeVita 12th ed. (line 123596): LV 400 mg/m2 concurrently with irinotecan.

drugs.name: Fluorouracil
drugs.notes: DeVita 12th ed. (line 123596-123597): followed by 5-FU bolus 400 mg/m2. Given as a separate line item from the infusional 5-FU dose below.

drugs.name: Fluorouracil
drugs.notes: DeVita 12th ed. (line 123597): 5-FU 1,200 mg/m2/d times 2 d (2,400 mg/m2 total infusion over 46-48 hr). dosePerUnit here is the per-day rate (1,200 mg/m2/day x 2 days = 2,400 mg/m2 total); days [1,2] reflects the 2-day infusion, not two separate bolus administrations.

premedications.name: Antiemetic prophylaxis
premedications.notes: per moderate emetic risk tier, see supportiveCare

supportiveCare: Antiemetics: moderate emetic risk tier (irinotecan is a moderate-emetic-risk IV agent per the NCCN 4-tier framework in Appendix D; 5-fluorouracil and leucovorin are low/minimal risk) - 5-HT3 antagonist +/- dexamethasone on treatment day per institutional antiemesis guideline

G-CSF: FOLFIRI is not a routinely-designated high-risk febrile-neutropenia regimen; per Appendix C, prophylactic CSF use for intermediate/unlisted-risk regimens is a physician-patient risk-benefit discussion, not a default order

Administration sequence per source: irinotecan given concurrently with leucovorin (same line via Y-connector), followed by 5-FU bolus, followed by 5-FU continuous infusion (Appendix F: order-of-administration language 'followed by' reflects the source-specified sequence)

monitoring: Renal and hepatic function (irinotecan is hepatically cleared; UGT1A1 status affects toxicity)

doseModificationRules.text: Review required. Protocol-specific delay/reduce criteria may apply; physician decides.

doseModificationRules.condition: UGT1A1*28 homozygous, hepatic dysfunction, or clinically significant irinotecan-related diarrhea
doseModificationRules.text: DeVita 12th ed. (Chapter 9, irinotecan pharmacology, lines 19427 to 19433): SN-38 is glucuronidated by UGT1A1; deficiency in this pathway increases the risk of diarrhea and myelosuppression, and dose reductions are recommended for patients homozygous for the UGT1A1*28 allele (a genotyping test is available) and for hepatic dysfunction with bilirubin greater than 1.5 (DeVita line 19433). Late diarrhea (onset beyond 24 hr after irinotecan) is managed with loperamide, escalating to diphenoxylate/atropine and opium tincture if severe (lines 19421 to 19426). Note: DeVita Chapter 40 (lines 121523 to 121531) states there are currently no specific guidelines for dose modification on the basis of UGT1A1 polymorphism in routine colorectal-cancer practice, so apply per physician judgement.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: Cancer of the Colon, Table 40.12; lines 123591, 123595, 123596, 123597. Setting/stage/intent from the same chapter's 'Management of Unresectable Metastatic Disease' section (lines 123342 to 123347, 123352), which contains Table 40.12.

provenanceNote: Textbook-grounded draft; NCCN per-disease template, clinical (StewardMD) review, and hospital/institutional approval pending. Resolved from DeVita 12th ed.: treatmentSetting=metastatic and stage IV from the 'Management of Unresectable Metastatic Disease' section (lines 123342 to 123343 heading; 'unresectable stage IV disease' line 123352) that contains Table 40.12 where this regimen appears; treatmentIntent=palliative from the same section (lines 123344 to 123347, 'Given the palliative nature of such treatments'). DeVita states there are no specific dose-modification guidelines based on UGT1A1 polymorphism (lines 121525 to 121528), so no UGT1A1 dose rule is added. histology, biomarkers, lineOfTherapy, and eligibilityCriteria stay VERIFY (not established for this regimen in DeVita), pending NCCN sourcing.
